intended_object: The right-hand side of the degree-one Mackey double coset formula in continuous cohomology: for open subgroups H (of finite index) and K of a topological group G, the map H¹(H, X) → H¹(K, X) given by Σ_{HxK ∈ H\G/K} cor^K_{K∩x⁻¹Hx} ∘ c_x ∘ res^H_{H∩xKx⁻¹}. H¹ is modelled as continuous crossed homomorphisms modulo principal ones. Inferred from the docstring, the module doc and the lemma `crossedQuotientRestrict_comp_transferQuotient_mackey`, which identifies it with res ∘ cor.
explanation:
The definition sums `mackeyDoubleCosetSummand X H K q` over all double cosets q ∈ H\G/K. The index set is finite because H has finite index (instance `mackeyDoubleCosetFinite`), and the `Fintype` instance obtained from `Fintype.ofFinite` only enables the finite sum.

Each summand is obtained with `Quotient.lift` from `mackeySummandQuotient X H K x`. That map is `transferQuotient` (corestriction) from `mackeyOpenStabilizer H K x` to K, composed with `mackeyConjugateQuotient`:
- The stabilizer is {l ∈ K | x l x⁻¹ ∈ H}, i.e. K ∩ x⁻¹Hx.
- The conjugation map sends f to l ↦ x⁻¹·f(x l x⁻¹). This is the standard conjugation-then-restriction map on H¹.

The library proves that the summand does not depend on the choice of transversal or of double-coset representative (h x b), so the lift is legitimate.

This is exactly the standard Mackey sum Σ_{x ∈ H\G/K} cor^K_{K∩x⁻¹Hx} ∘ c_x ∘ res. The library uses it as the right-hand side of res^G_K ∘ cor^G_H in its degree-one Mackey formula.

The setting is general and matches the literature for continuous cohomology: any topological ring k, any topological group G, open subgroups with H of finite index, and jointly continuous coefficients. Restricting to degree one through the crossed-homomorphism model is the declared scope of the file, not an artificial narrowing of this particular sum. Mathlib has no continuous-cohomology Mackey formula to compare against.
